To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNA methylation and chromatin remodeling are important during preimplantational development of swine embryos.

(1) DNA methylation and the expression of DNA methyltransferases are dynamic during preimplantational development of porcine embryos; (2) histone modification is also dynamic during preimplatational development of porine embryos; and (3) assisted epigenetic remodeling of the donor nucleus and the SCNTE embryo improves the cloning efficiency of porcine SCNT embryos.

(i) DNA methylation is an important regulator of gene expression during swine embryonic development; (ii) the methylation pattern of the donor cell nucleus is not maintained during the early developmental stages of SCNT embryos; (iii) DNA methylation patterns are reprogrammed during the first cell cycle after SCNT; and (iv) the reprogramming process is incomplete in SCNT embryos and is associated with a lower rate of development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epigenetic regulation of gene expression in swine embryos, and the effects of this regulation on cloning by SCNT.
the mechanisms of epigenetic control during preimplantational development and the effect of these epigenetic events on the cloning efficiency of SCNT embryos.
the epigenetic mechanisms that regulate the development of embryos derived either from fertilization or from SCNT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
epigenetic remodeling is a complex process that is incompletely understood, and that it remains a major hurdle to overcome for the successful application of SCNT technology to swine.
epigenetic regulation is important in the development of embryos and in cloning by SCNT.
epigenetic regulation is essential for normal preimplantation embryo development, but that it is not fully understood and requires further study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DNA methylation and chromatin remodeling play important roles during swine embryonic development and SCNT, and that assisted epigenetic modification of donor cells and SCNT embryos may help to improve cloning efficiency and offspring quality.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the epigenetic remodeling process during preimplantational development and SCNT is a complex process involving many epigenetic modifications.
epigenetic regulation and remodeling are important for successful SCNT.
